# Drakar

> A native macOS app to drive Claude Code: the conversation, the tool calls, the permission
> prompts and the diffs, in a window as light as Zed. It runs the `claude` you installed over its
> stream-json protocol, the way the VS Code extension does, and a session can run Codex instead,
> through its `app-server`. Nothing is bundled, imported or synced.

Released: a Developer ID signed, notarized zip published on GitHub releases, downloadable at
https://drakar.mgcrea.io/download, with a licence at https://drakar.mgcrea.io/buy. macOS 26 or
later, and macOS only. Open source under the MIT licence at https://github.com/mgcrea/drakar.
Not affiliated with Anthropic or OpenAI.

## The conversation

- Each turn as it arrives: text, thinking, Markdown, and every tool call as a card with its result.
  Edit and Write calls show their diffs.
- Permission prompts, the agent's questions and an MCP server's questions are answered in their
  card; a yes-or-no one also from the toolbar, with ⌥⌘Y or ⌥⌘N.
- A subagent's card shows its whole conversation. A running task can be stopped, sent to the
  background, and its output read.
- Rewind and fork from any prompt: fork the conversation from there, rewind the files Claude
  changed since, or both, with the files and line counts shown before anything changes.
- What you select in the editor, or the file you have open, goes with your next prompt. ⌥K pins
  a selection as a chip so another can be added beside it.

## The editor

- A session window shows its folder's files and opens them as tabs beside the conversation, with
  line numbers and colours. ⌘S saves, ⌘P finds a file by name, ⇧⌘F searches the folder.
- A tab the agent changes reloads; if you edited it too, Drakar asks which version to keep, and it
  asks before a window with unsaved tabs closes.
- While Drakar runs, a `claude --ide` in a terminal, in a folder Drakar has open (or connected
  with `/ide`), sends every edit to Drakar's Review Changes window, and the file is written only
  if you accept it there.

## Sessions

- The sidebar sorts what needs you first; ⌥⌘↑ and ⌥⌘↓ move between sessions, and Next After
  Replying shows the next one waiting.
- Sessions across `~/.claude` and every `~/.claude-*` account. Settings › General picks which
  `claude` runs and the account (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) a new session starts under.
- A small helper holds the `claude` and `codex` processes, so a quit, a crash or an update leaves
  them working; the next launch attaches and replays what they did meanwhile.
- Sessions a terminal or VS Code runs show their state in the sidebar and can be moved into the
  window. Mark several (or Mark All Sessions, ⌥⌘A) and send them one prompt, or run a skill in a
  session per subfolder.
- A Skills window lists both agents' skills, commands and plugins, installed from a git address
  or a folder.

## Privacy and security

- Drakar listens on one network socket, on 127.0.0.1, which answers only a client holding this
  launch's token (the IDE bridge), and its session host on one Unix socket, which only your own
  Drakar can reach.
- The only connections Drakar opens of its own are Sparkle's, to check for and fetch updates,
  and only once you said yes to update checks. A check reads drakar.mgcrea.io/appcast.xml and
  sends no identifier. Everything else that reaches the network is the `claude` or `codex` you
  installed.
- The licence key is checked on your Mac, never by a server. No analytics, no telemetry, no crash
  reporter.
- No entitlements and no sandbox, by design: it spawns agents that work on your files. Hardened
  runtime on every binary. `make audit`, `make audit-running` and `make audit-release` check the
  claim against the sources, the running app and the built bundle.
